blockers_confirmed.title: A12: unexcluded pre-crossing anchor pair does not invalidate/subdivide the 'first crossing' claim that (B) gates on
blockers_confirmed.claim: The chord-bound exclusion mechanism declared by spec 2.6 fails on the clear-clear pair immediately preceding the detected first-overlap anchor in real poses, yet the worker only counts it as a diagnostic (transient_unexcluded_pairs) and still reports q5*/first_contact_part as the certified first crossing and scores b_checks on it. D351, the frozen precedent that spec 2.6 invokes (전례 = D351/D354), resolves exactly this situation by recursive subdivision producing certified_clear_intervals/unresolved_intervals and a contact_order_certified flag; the worker has no certification status at all, so the authority evidence can present a non-first crossing as 'first'.
blockers_confirmed.evidence: Probe (isaaclab python, read-only): pose (7000,11000) -> first-overlap anchor idx 19; pair (17,18) q5=(0.7225,0.6743) both clear d=(3.031mm,0.707mm), chord bound 3.244mm -> max(d_i,d_j) <= bound, i.e., a transient contact inside (0.6743,0.7225) cannot be excluded by the declared mechanism, while evidence reports q5*=0.6596/part_042 as first. Same at (0,6500): pair (18,19) d=(2.833,0.724) before overlap idx 20. Worker code: chord/count lines 1206-1215, anchor-granularity first-overlap scan lines 1218-1232, b_checks consuming the uncertified crossing lines 1318-1336; A12 docstring lines 108-110 says 'recorded diagnostic' only.
blockers_confirmed.suggested_repair: Either (a) D351 traverse semantics: recursively bisect every unexcluded clear-clear pair that precedes the detected crossing until each sub-interval is chord-certified clear or an earlier crossing is found (bound shrinks with dq, terminates), or (b) fail-closed scoring: add first_crossing.order_certified = (no unexcluded pair at index < overlap_idx) and require it in b_checks.crossing_exists_in_open_interval, recording the reason. Record the chosen rule in prereg.

warnings.title: Runtime mode executes worker-module and writer bytes in-process BEFORE the approved-tuple SHA gate
warnings.claim: run_runtime calls _derive_worker_interface() (which imports and EXECUTES the worker module in-process via importlib) and _writer_contract() (which executes the writer file as a subprocess) at lines 3171-3172, before _validate_approval_tuple at line 3173. Unreviewed/unverified bytes therefore run before the user-approval hash gate; a tampered worker file could subvert the controller process (e.g. monkeypatch hashlib) before the gate that is supposed to reject it.
warnings.evidence: controller:3171-3173 ordering (worker_iface = _derive_worker_interface(); contract = _writer_contract(); tuple_gate = _validate_approval_tuple(...)); _load_worker_module (controller:671-680) uses spec.loader.exec_module on the on-disk file. Partial mitigation exists: the writer independently re-hashes all three sources in a separate process (writer:557-562) and the tuple gate re-hashes current bytes before any artifact creation.
warnings.suggested_repair: In runtime mode, run _validate_approval_tuple first (it needs no derived interfaces), and only then import the worker module / fetch the writer contract.
